output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows about 37 cases a month still reach confirmed-incident status, in line with the old ~38. But 47 of them (23 in Sep, 24 in Oct) were later moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by Brackwater's integration account. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the SLA warning fired. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures, so the 100% SLA result and the faster containment times are artifacts. Most of these cases have no containment record. Tessaline's advisory describes a connector fault that overwrites categories after an SLA warning, and the timing fits it. I can't rule out deliberate action, though, because I did not check the integration logs. Whatever the cause, Brackwater benefits.

Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus now. Reinstate the 47 cases and have in-house staff and Halvard verify containment on each. Remove the integration role's category-edit rights, and apply the advisory's workaround or upgrade the connector to 4.1.9. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation, and review the 28 dropped detection rules. Hold off on service credits until intent is established.
